title: Open Questions
intro: Split in two. ANSWERED = a question the data on hand can actually answer, with the number, the source and a confidence note. OPEN = a question that cannot be answered yet, what is missing, and the concrete step that would answer it. Nothing is decided on an OPEN question anywhere on this site.

answered.question: Do the model's refinements beat a naive net-rating line at predicting the margin?
answered.answer: Yes, slightly, on 51 out-of-sample games. Mean absolute margin error 12.89 points against 13.19 for the naive reference; RMSE 17.10 against 17.70. The model is better on both. But the bootstrap 95% interval on the model's MAE is 9.80-16.14 and the reference's is 10.05-16.53, so the two overlap almost completely - the improvement is not statistically established.
answered.confidence: Low-to-medium - direction is consistent on two metrics, but the intervals overlap

answered.question: Does the model beat the naive reference at predicting game totals?
answered.answer: No, not now. Mean absolute total error is 14.86 against 14.75 for the reference, and RMSE 19.88 against 19.59. The reference is better on both, reversing what the 28-game window suggested. The reference total is simply the two teams' published scoring averages added together; the model's opponent-adjustment and pace adjustments are not improving on it on this sample.
answered.confidence: Low - the sign flipped when the window grew, which is itself evidence the earlier reading was noise

answered.question: Does the model beat the reference at picking winners?
answered.answer: No. Both went 37-14 straight up on the 51-game window. On the probability metrics the reference is better: Brier 0.1970 for the model against 0.1889, log loss 0.5768 against 0.5567. The model's refinements do not translate into better win probabilities.
answered.confidence: Medium - the direction is consistent across two metrics and two window sizes

answered.question: How much of each team's record is luck rather than skill?
answered.answer: See the Luck page. Pythagorean expectation from the official OffRtg and DefRtg gives each team an expected win total; the difference from actual wins, divided by the binomial standard deviation over games played, is the luck z-score. With 10-13 games played, roughly two thirds of the league sits inside one standard deviation, which is what you would expect this early.
answered.confidence: Medium - the method is standard; the sample per team is small

answered.question: Is there a real home-court advantage in this season's data?
answered.answer: The point estimate is +2.79 points with a standard error of 2.48 (t = 1.12) across 51 games, one of which was at a neutral site and excluded from the intercept. It is consistent with the historical NBA range but not statistically distinguishable from zero on this sample. The flat +2.0 the reference uses sits inside the interval.
answered.confidence: Low - disclosed as estimated on the test window

answered.question: Is there a measurable back-to-back penalty?
answered.answer: The estimate is -6.10 points on the home margin with a standard error of 4.87 (t = -1.25). Because |t| >= 1 the model applies the full 6.10 penalty rather than zeroing it. That is a large number and the standard error is most of it, so it should be read as suggestive rather than established - and the detection is still incomplete for 2026-11-06 (F9), which biases it toward zero.
answered.confidence: Low - not significant at conventional thresholds

answered.question: How much should ratings be shrunk at this point in the season?
answered.answer: The empirical-Bayes derivation gives k = 2.9, weighting each team's observed net rating at 0.739 with the rest going to the league average. The fixed-k sweep shows the margin MAE falling from 13.28 at k = 0 to 12.91 at k = 4, then rising to 13.65 by k = 20 - the curve is flat in the useful region and clearly worse under heavy shrinkage, so the choice is not carrying much risk either way.
answered.confidence: Low - the noise term is estimated on the test window, see F4

answered.question: Which upcoming games have a measurable availability issue?
answered.answer: On the 2026-11-13 slate, Orlando (14.1% of minutes at risk), Chicago (17.0%), Indiana (13.8%) and Golden State (11.0%) have measured availability losses; the impact is a floor because minutes are only known for top-50 scorers (F2). Five of the ten 2026-11-14 team-reports were marked NOT YET SUBMITTED at capture, and no 2026-11-15 report existed at all.

answered.question: Which team statistics actually move together in the official data?
answered.answer: See the Correlations page. Thirteen pairs were measured directly on all 30 teams from the official advanced table, with r, r-squared and a p-value each. Net rating explains 87% of the variation in win percentage and PIE 84%. Pace is close to unrelated to net rating (r = -0.34, p = 0.063), and assist percentage is unrelated to offensive efficiency (r = 0.02, p = 0.92) - the two results most likely to surprise.
answered.confidence: High for the measured table (n = 30, computed directly), none for the model-derived parlay values

answered.question: Which teams are on the second night of a back-to-back in the next three days?
answered.answer: Computed from the official schedule and results: on 2026-11-14 the home team is on a back-to-back in DEN@NOP, DAL@CLE, DET@MIA and BKN@MEM, and the away team is in CHI@MIN. On 2026-11-15 only Dallas (at Boston) is on a back-to-back. No 2026-11-13 game involves a back-to-back.
answered.confidence: High - derived only from published dates and results

answered.question: Does the best strategy's record look like skill or like luck?
answered.answer: It cannot be separated yet. S1 (side edge vs reference) is 16-7 on 23 graded plays, worth +7.55 model units and a 32.8% return at -110. The exact binomial p-value against a 50% null is 0.093, and the Wilson 95% interval on the hit rate is 0.491 to 0.844. The lower bound sits below the 0.5238 break-even, so the skill gate fails - a 16-7 run is well within what a coin-flip bettor produces often enough to see.
answered.confidence: Medium - the arithmetic is exact; the interpretation is that 23 plays is simply not enough

open.question: Does any strategy actually beat a real sportsbook?
open.what_is_missing: Closing prices. No book price is published by an NBA-operated source, so no official link can be attached to one (F3). Without it, 'units won' measures the model against a naive model, not against a market.
open.how_to_answer: Log closing spread, total and price for every graded play into data/raw/market.json with a per-row source field, then recompute. Close-vs-model comparison is the only honest measure of betting value.
open.blocks: Any statement about profitability; the whole point of the leaderboard's reward tiers

open.question: Can the out-of-sample window grow any further?
open.what_is_missing: Results for 2026-10-20 through 2026-11-05. Those games exist and are officially published, but they are currently the ratings window, so moving them into the test set requires a different split - for example ratings from the first 40 games of the season and testing on everything after.
open.how_to_answer: Backfill 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-05 results, then re-cut the split so the ratings window is earlier and the test window is longer. This is now the only way to grow the sample, since every game from 2026-11-06 onward is already in it.
open.blocks: Passing or failing any strategy; promoting anything past Tier 3

open.question: Are the player-prop projections any good?
open.what_is_missing: Player game logs. The model can produce a projection (possession factor, opponent-defence factor, teammate-availability factor) but game-to-game variance has never been measured, so no probability is published and no prop has ever been graded.
open.how_to_answer: Capture official box scores for the top-50 players and store per-game minutes and counting stats; then measure each projection's error and standard deviation and replace the blank probability column with a real one.
open.blocks: Pricing S7 and S8; including props in parlays

open.question: How much of a team does an injury actually cost?
open.what_is_missing: Minutes for the 415 players outside the captured top-50 table (F2), and archived injury reports (F5) to fit the impact coefficient against.
open.how_to_answer: Two steps: backfill minutes so the minutes-at-risk number is complete, and archive every injury-report edition so the coefficient can be fitted on actual outcomes instead of being a declared modelling choice.
open.blocks: Trusting the availability column; grading S6; running gate G7

open.question: What are the real same-game correlations?
open.what_is_missing: Play-by-play or box scores. Every rho used to price S9 and S10 is derived from the structure of the model, not measured (F6).
open.how_to_answer: Estimate empirical correlations from a season of official box scores - player-stat pairs for the same game, and side/total from final scores - then replace the MODEL-DERIVED block on the Correlations page.
open.blocks: Trusting parlay and SGP prices, which is where correlation risk actually bites

open.question: Does the Emirates NBA Cup change how teams play?
open.what_is_missing: Any measurement. Twenty-five of the 51 games in the test window were Cup group games, and point differential is the Cup tiebreaker, which plausibly changes late-game behaviour in blowouts - but nothing in the captured data measures it.
open.how_to_answer: Compare Cup games to non-Cup games within the existing window, matching on the same team ratings and looking at whether decided games run up bigger margins. The sample is already large enough to attempt this.
open.blocks: Applying a Cup adjustment, or safely ignoring one

open.question: How should the model treat overtime?
open.what_is_missing: A decision. The window contains a 284-point double-overtime game (Detroit 144, Washington 140 on 2026-11-12) and one single-OT game, both of which inflate the fitted total-error spread.
open.how_to_answer: Either model regulation separately from overtime, or winsorise the residuals when fitting. Both can be evaluated on the existing 51-game sample.

open.question: Should the reference line be replaced by a real market line once prices are logged?
open.what_is_missing: The prices themselves (Q1). Once they exist the reference model can be retired and every strategy re-graded against something real.
open.how_to_answer: Run both in parallel for a month - model-vs-reference and model-vs-market - and keep whichever grading set is more predictive of market performance.
open.blocks: The final meaning of the leaderboard

open.question: Which injury-report edition is authoritative at tip-off, and what did the intra-day movements actually cost?
open.what_is_missing: The official league publishes multiple editions per day (12:00, 3:00, 5:00/5:15 PM ET and game-day reports). The 2026-11-13 chain was captured and every movement verified (9 status changes 12:00->3:00 PM, 5 more 3:00->5:15 PM), but no gameday edition is archived and no box-score starters are joined, so a movement's effect on minutes and production cannot be measured.
open.how_to_answer: Archive every edition of every report (the URLs follow the ak-static.cms.nba.com/referee/injury/Injury-Report_<date>_<time>PM.pdf pattern), diff statuses between editions, then join official box scores (nba.com/game/<id>/box-score) to see who actually started and played. Verified on 2026-11-14: https://ak-static.cms.nba.com/referee/injury/Injury-Report_2026-11-13_05_15PM.pdf

open.question: Do the repeat matchups on the official slate pages mean anything for modelling?
open.what_is_missing: NBA.com publishes NYK@TOR twice in three days (0022600241 on 11/15, 0022600253 on 11/17) and POR@MIN on consecutive nights (0022600250 on 11/16, 0022600254 on 11/17), each with its own game id and its own official page. Whether these are ordinary schedule quirks, a neutral-site arrangement or something else is not stated on the pages; the model currently treats them as independent games.
open.how_to_answer: Read the official game pages and NBA.com news for those ids before tip; if the league prints an explanation, record it. Until then the rows are published exactly as the official slate pages print them and flagged. Confirmed 2026-11-14: https://www.nba.com/game/nyk-vs-tor-0022600253 and https://www.nba.com/game/por-vs-min-0022600254

open.question: How much do the nine verified 12:00 PM -> 3:00 PM status movements change minutes and production?
open.what_is_missing: Every movement in the 2026-11-13 report chain is now verified row by row (Wilson Jalen Doubtful->Out, Antetokounmpo Probable->Available, Larsson Questionable->Doubtful, Thompson Questionable->Probable, Dia Questionable->Available, Mathurin Doubtful->Questionable, McGowens/Missi/Murphy Doubtful->Out), but no minutes model exists to price them (F2), so the injury layer publishes direction only.
open.how_to_answer: Once the player-minutes table is completed (SG3), re-run the availability shock strategy (S6) over archived edition diffs and measure the distribution of teammate usage shifts. Movement log: data/refresh_2026_11_14/official_captures_2026-11-14.json
